newsitem.title: UK: Trans-World has put Russian investment on hold.
newsitem.headline: Trans-World has put Russian investment on hold.

text.p: Trans-World Group investments in Russia are on hold until the Russian government announces an official position on a minister's call to curb foreign ownership of the aluminium industry, a director of the firm said on Friday.
"We want to see an official position by the government before we continue our investment programme in Russia," said Mel Wilde, director at Trans-World (Steel) Ltd.
Aluminium deliveries were not affected at present, Wilde told reporters at a conference on commercial opportunities in the CIS, organised by the Adam Smith Institute.
Late last month Russian Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov told the Duma that domestic aluminium producers should be protected from Western tolling companies.
Trans-World is a major player in this market, importing alumina from the West which is refined into aluminium in Russia and then exported.
The company has met with U.K. Foreign Office officials and is seeking meetings with the U.S. State Department and Russia's Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to clarify the issue.
Earlier this week, Trans-World executive Chairman David Reuben announced that the company is looking to invest $500 million in Russia's Bratsk and Sayansk smelters to raise output in coming years.
